themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retailer Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints spiked to 9 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 1.9 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 380% increase (z-score: 3.63)—signaling potential unauthorized or problematic retail operations emerging in East Harlem.
evidence: 9 cannabis retailer complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.9 weekly baseline (380% spike, z-score: 3.63)
Sharp acceleration suggests new unlicensed operations or license violations in the district
Pattern distinct from other safety complaints, indicating a concentrated issue
reporting_angles: Investigate whether complaints are tied to specific unlicensed retailers or compliance issues at licensed shops
Interview residents and local business owners about what types of violations they're reporting (noise, odor, foot traffic, etc.)

themes_detail.label: Encampment & Drug Activity Spike
themes_detail.summary: Over the past week, encampment complaints jumped to 12 (540% above the 1.9 weekly baseline) and drug activity complaints hit 9 (279% above 2.4 average)—the largest coordinated public safety cluster in recent weeks, suggesting worsening street conditions.
evidence: Encampment complaints: 12 last week vs. 1.9 weekly average (540% spike, z-score: 5.99)
Drug activity complaints: 9 last week vs. 2.4 weekly average (279% spike, z-score: 4.2)
Two correlated safety issues emerging simultaneously suggests systemic street-level deterioration
reporting_angles: Map the geographic distribution of encampments and drug complaints to identify hotspots and clustering patterns
Interview residents, business owners, and outreach workers about triggers for the increase and access to shelter/services

themes_detail.label: Sanitation Crisis: Dead Animals & Litter
themes_detail.summary: This week, dead animal complaints reached 4 (1500% above 0.2 weekly baseline) and litter basket requests hit 3 (2300% above 0.1 average)—the highest statistical anomalies across all 311 categories, indicating acute sanitation degradation.
evidence: Dead animal complaints: 4 THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (1500% spike, z-score: 8.66, severity: high)
Litter basket requests: 3 THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69, severity: high)
Consistent community board budget request for graffiti removal/cleaning indicates years of unmet sanitation needs
reporting_angles: Investigate whether DSNY staffing or collection schedules have been reduced; request response times for dead animal removal
Report on residents' daily experience with sanitation failures and health/safety concerns from uncollected waste

themes_detail.label: Graffiti and Visual Disorder Escalation
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints jumped to 5 last week (700% above 0.6 weekly baseline, z-score: 3.94), coinciding with noise complaints up 178% to 47 (vs. 16.9 average)—a convergence of disorder signals that mirrors the district's long-standing budget requests for graffiti removal.
evidence: Graffiti complaints: 5 last week vs. 0.6 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 3.94, severity: high)
Noise complaints: 47 last week vs. 16.9 weekly average (178% spike, z-score: 3.82, severity: high)
Community board has repeatedly requested increased graffiti removal funding—suggests chronic under-resourcing and deteriorating conditions
reporting_angles: Examine DSNY graffiti removal response times and capacity constraints in CD 111 relative to other districts
Assess whether visual disorder and noise are linked to the encampment and drug activity surges

themes_detail.label: Noise Complaints at Two-Year High
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints (residential + street/sidewalk combined) reached approximately 47 this past week, representing a 178% increase over the 8-week baseline of 16.9 weekly—the largest spike in the noise category and one of the highest on the 311 roster.
evidence: Noise complaints: 47 last week vs. 16.9 weekly average (178% spike, z-score: 3.82)
Noise remains second-largest complaint category overall (2,117 over 90 days), now accelerating sharply
Community board budget request for traffic enforcement agents reflects ongoing noise/quality-of-life concerns
reporting_angles: Interview residents about the types of noise (traffic, construction, street activity, nightlife) contributing to the spike
Determine whether noise complaints correlate with encampments or street-level activity increases
